claims.statement: Generational depth-3 formation exists in two shapes (c3 pure-run m3=(m2,m2); c4/c5 separator m3=(m2,c,m2)), each macro body literally referencing the previous generation, GRW-1-exact; under the frozen INV-1 rule formation SATURATES at depth 3 (separator-pair dominance gain(u c u) - gain(u) = P*n - b - 1 > 0 and run-internal k in {X/2, X} dominance; designed depth-4/5 corpora stop at 3), and the ceiling is rule-attributable (ADM-ALT smallest-body diagnostic reaches depth 7/9 on the same corpora at the same charges). Held-out burden reduction COMPOUNDS with depth only tier-conditionally: strictly decreasing to the matching generation, strictly regressing below it, controls strictly regressing throughout.
assumptions: frozen {a,b,c}+concatenation grammar, INV-1 charged greedy admission unchanged from v1
tier suites frozen before any tranche-2 run; honest-failure clauses in fixtures
corpus mass per depth level is a derived output (f* bracket scans), not a tuned constant
falsifiers: any depth-4 corpus under INV-1 (none found; c4/c5 designed for depth 4/5 stop at 3)
any tier whose burden series violates the monotone-then-regress pattern
oracle disagreement on any tier row or trace
claims.limits: existence + mechanism at registered scope only; no claim that depth 3 is optimal for other rules (ADM-ALT goes deeper), no open-ended growth, no claim beyond the frozen cost model

claims.statement: Neither compression-gated (INV-1) nor utility-gated (UTL-1) admission dominates under the same charged burden metric with the same nulls. Compression regresses against primitive-only search exactly when corpus compressibility diverges from held-out reuse (trap3: greedy 'abc' admission destroys the reusable 'ab' occurrence mass; net +43897 > 0, and 52/200 random nulls beat the compression arm on trap1 while 0/200 beat the utility arm). The utility gate forfeits deep-macro gains when the validation suite under-represents deep reuse (c3 + shallow V: compression better by 14939; with a deep V: exact tie). The g2-acquisition-economics warning is confirmed head-on and extended with the converse failure direction (validation-suiteness is a distinct axis).
assumptions: UTL-1 gate uses the frozen disjoint validation suites; V influencing admission is the gate's function, not leakage (HLK-2 hostile)
both arms charged fully (definition + maintenance) at kappa=1
same burden metric, same 200-seed null protocol per arm
falsifiers: a corpus where either rule dominates across all six registered corpora (none: ties on v1ref/c4/c5, split on c3/traps)
utility gate admitting the full chain under the shallow V (it does not)
leakage from eval suites into either arm (HLK-2: byte-identical libraries)
claims.limits: six frozen corpora and one gate family at registered scope; no claim about optimal admission rules, no universal ranking of gates

claims.statement: Under the frozen EXEC-B per-op cost model (base token = 1 op, macro = rho + body cost; primary rho = 1), the v1 headline survives: H+ exec net -395484/-393054/-388194 at rho = 1/2/4 (count metric -48739), H- regression preserved, exact break-even rho-dagger = 164. The survival is cost-model-relative, not uniform: 19/200 equal-size nulls beat the true recursive library under EXEC-B(1) (flat 'abab' executes in 5 ops vs recursive m2 in 7), so the v1 net claim is robust while the v1 rank-1 null claim is cost-fragile. All head-to-head and tier verdicts agree in sign between count and exec metrics.
assumptions: EXEC-B frozen before implementation (no memoization, unit base cost, rho grid {1,2,4} + break-even scan to 1024)
enumerator unchanged (breadth-by-length, lexicographic); only the accounting changes
falsifiers: exec DP vs naive enumeration mismatch (none on the battery)
sign flip of any verdict between count and exec metrics at rho in grid (none)
break-even rho below the grid (it is 164)
claims.limits: one per-op cost family; no claim for arbitrary cost models (forbidden promotion EXEC_INVARIANT_ALL_RHO); rank conclusion specific to EXEC-B(1)
